chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Knowledge dispels the excuse of those who advance excuses.
ai.seo_question: How does knowledge remove excuses according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this maxim from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) asserts that genuine knowledge (*'ilm*) nullifies the plea of ignorance (*'udhr*) for those who attempt to excuse their negligence or sins. This principle underscores the Shia scholarly view that accountability is contingent upon the availability of knowledge, meaning that true understanding removes the veil of excuse, compelling individuals to act upon what they know. It serves as a foundational criterion for distinguishing between the excusable novice and the accountable scholar in Islamic jurisprudence.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 284. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
Knowledge dispels the excuse of those who advance excuses.
